items.title: The Form Realm's Pleasure, Dhyāna by Dhyāna

items.zh: 復次，於色界中初靜慮地受生諸天，即受彼地離生喜樂。第二靜慮地諸天，受定生喜樂。
items.en: Further, the gods reborn in the first dhyāna of the form realm experience that very ground's joy and bliss born of seclusion. The gods of the second dhyāna experience joy and bliss born of concentration.

items.zh: 第三靜慮地諸天，受離喜妙樂。第四靜慮地諸天，受捨念清淨寂靜無動之樂。
items.en: The gods of the third dhyāna experience the sublime bliss free of joy. The gods of the fourth dhyāna experience the still, unmoving bliss of purified equanimity and mindfulness.

items.title: The Formless Realm's Pleasure of Release

items.zh: 無色界諸天，受極寂靜解脫之樂。
items.en: The gods of the formless realm experience the most utterly still pleasure of release.

items.title: Six Ways Suffering and Pleasure Scale Across the Realms

items.zh: 又由六種殊勝故，苦樂殊勝應知。一、形量殊勝，二、柔軟殊勝，三、緣殊勝，四、時殊勝，五、心殊勝，六、所依殊勝。
items.en: Further, it should be understood that suffering and pleasure themselves become more intense by reason of six distinguishing factors: first, the distinction of bodily size; second, the distinction of bodily softness; third, the distinction of conditions; fourth, the distinction of duration; fifth, the distinction of mind; sixth, the distinction of underlying basis.

items.title: Why Each of the Six Makes Suffering — and Pleasure — More Intense

items.zh: 何以故？如如身量漸增廣大，如是如是苦轉殊勝；如如依止漸更柔軟，如是如是苦轉殊勝；如如苦緣漸更猛盛眾多差別，如是如是苦轉殊勝；
items.en: Why is this? The more a being's bodily size gradually increases, the more intense its suffering becomes. The more its bodily basis grows gradually softer, the more intense its suffering becomes. The more the conditions of its suffering grow gradually more intense and more numerous in kind, the more intense its suffering becomes.

items.zh: 如如時分漸遠無間，如是如是苦轉殊勝；如如內心無簡擇力漸漸增廣，如是如是苦轉殊勝；如如所依苦器漸增，如是如是苦轉殊勝。
items.en: The more the duration of its suffering gradually extends without interruption, the more intense its suffering becomes. The more its mind's power of discernment gradually diminishes, the more intense its suffering becomes. The more its underlying vessel of suffering gradually increases, the more intense its suffering becomes.

items.zh: 如苦殊勝如是，樂殊勝義隨其所應，廣說應知。
items.en: As with the intensification of suffering, so, in due correspondence, should the intensification of pleasure be understood at length.

items.zh: 又樂有二種：一、非聖財所生樂，二、聖財所生樂。

items.title: Four Ordinary Resources That Produce Pleasure

items.zh: 非聖財所生樂者，謂四種資具為緣得生。一、適悅資具，二、滋長資具，三、清淨資具，四、住持資具。
items.en: Pleasure not born of noble wealth arises in dependence on four kinds of resource: first, resources of delight; second, resources of nourishment; third, resources of good omen; fourth, resources of sustenance.

items.zh: 適悅資具者，謂車乘、衣服、諸莊嚴具、歌笑舞樂、塗香花鬘、種種上妙珍翫樂具、光明照曜、男女侍衛、種種庫藏。
items.en: Resources of delight are: conveyances, clothing, every kind of ornament, song and laughter and dance and music, scented oils and garlands, every manner of fine and wondrous plaything, bright illumination, male and female attendants, and every kind of storehouse of goods.

items.zh: 滋長資具者，謂無尋思輪石椎打、築蹋、按摩等事。清淨資具者，謂吉祥草、頻螺果、螺貝滿瓮等事。住持資具者，謂飲及食。
items.en: Resources of nourishment are: being struck with a mindless roller or stone, being pounded, being trodden upon, being massaged, and the like. Resources of good omen are: auspicious grass, the bilva fruit, jars filled with conch shells, and the like. Resources of sustenance are drink and food.

items.zh: 聖財所生樂者，謂七聖財為緣得生。何等為七？一、信，二、戒，三、慚，四、愧，五、聞，六、捨，七、慧。
items.en: Pleasure born of noble wealth arises in dependence on the seven kinds of noble wealth. What are these seven? Faith, moral discipline, conscientiousness, a sense of shame, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

items.title: Fifteen Ways Noble Wealth Outshines Ordinary Wealth, Part One

items.zh: 復次，由十五種相，聖非聖財所生樂差別。何等十五？謂非聖財所生樂能起惡行，聖財所生樂能起妙行。
items.en: Further, noble and non-noble wealth's pleasure differ by fifteen distinguishing features. Non-noble wealth's pleasure can give rise to unwholesome conduct; noble wealth's pleasure can give rise to excellent conduct.

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，有罪喜樂相應；聖財所生樂，無罪喜樂相應。又非聖財所生樂，微小不遍所依；聖財所生樂，廣大遍滿所依。
items.en: Non-noble wealth's pleasure is associated with blameworthy delight; noble wealth's pleasure is associated with blameless delight. Non-noble wealth's pleasure is slight, never pervading its basis fully; noble wealth's pleasure is vast, pervading its basis completely.

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，非一切時有，以依外緣故；聖財所生樂，一切時有，以依內緣故。又非聖財所生樂，非一切地有，唯欲界故；聖財所生樂，一切地有，通三界繫及不繫故。
items.en: Non-noble wealth's pleasure is not present at all times, since it depends on external conditions; noble wealth's pleasure is present at all times, since it depends on internal conditions. Non-noble wealth's pleasure is not present in every ground, existing only in the desire realm; noble wealth's pleasure is present in every ground, extending through all three realms, whether one is still bound by them or already free.

items.title: Fifteen Ways Noble Wealth Outshines Ordinary Wealth, Part Two

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，不能引發後世聖非聖財；聖財所生樂，能引發後世聖非聖財。
items.en: Non-noble wealth's pleasure cannot give rise to noble or non-noble wealth in a future life; noble wealth's pleasure can give rise to both noble and non-noble wealth in a future life.

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，若受用時，有盡有邊；聖財所生樂，若受用時，轉更充盛，增長廣大。
items.en: Non-noble wealth's pleasure, when enjoyed, is exhaustible and has a limit; noble wealth's pleasure, when enjoyed, only grows fuller and more abundant, expanding without bound.

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，為他劫奪，若王、若賊、怨，及水、火；聖財所生樂，無能侵奪。
items.en: Non-noble wealth's pleasure can be seized by others — by a king, a thief, an enemy, by flood or by fire; noble wealth's pleasure can be seized by nothing at all.

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，不可從今世持往後世；聖財所生樂，可從今世持往後世。又非聖財所生樂，受用之時不可充足；聖財所生樂，受用之時究竟充滿。
items.en: Non-noble wealth's pleasure cannot be carried from this life into the next; noble wealth's pleasure can be carried from this life into the next. Non-noble wealth's pleasure, however much it is enjoyed, can never be fully satisfied; noble wealth's pleasure, when enjoyed, is completely and utterly fulfilling.

items.zh: 又非聖財所生樂，有怖畏、有怨對、有災橫、有燒惱、不能斷後世大苦。

items.title: The Last Five of Fifteen Contrasts

items.zh: 有怖畏者，謂懼當生苦所依處故。有怨對者：謂鬪訟違諍所依處故。有災橫者，謂老病死所依處故。
items.en: Carrying dread means it is the basis for fearing a future birth into suffering. Carrying enmity means it is the basis for quarrels, litigation, and conflict. Carrying calamity means it is the basis for old age, sickness, and death.

items.zh: 有燒惱者，謂由此樂性不真實，如疥癩病，虛妄顛倒所依處故，愁歎憂苦種種熱惱所依處故。不能斷後世大苦者，謂貪瞋等本隨二惑所依處故。
items.en: Carrying affliction means that, its very nature being unreal, like scabies or leprosy, it is the basis for delusion and distortion, and the basis for sorrow, lamentation, and every kind of burning distress. Being unable to sever the great suffering of a future life means it is the basis for the root afflictions and their secondary forms alike, such as craving and hatred.

items.zh: 聖財所生樂，無怖畏、無怨對、無災橫、無燒惱、能斷後世大苦。
items.en: Noble wealth's pleasure carries no dread, no enmity, no calamity, no affliction, and is capable of severing the great suffering of a future life.

items.zh: 隨其所應，與上相違，廣說應知。

blocks.text: Fascicle 5 continues the survey of enjoyment that fascicle 4 began. Today the treatise describes the pleasures of meditation in the form and formless realms, explains why both suffering and pleasure grow more intense in some lives than others, and then makes a contrast that every Buddhist teacher returns to: ordinary wealth against **noble wealth**, the seven inner treasures of the practitioner.

Three short passages are untranslated: 0299a21 (pleasure is of two kinds, born of non-noble wealth and born of noble wealth), 0299b20 (pleasure from non-noble wealth brings fear, enmity, calamity, and torment, and cannot cut off great suffering in later lives), and 0299b29 ("for the rest, the opposite should be understood at length").
Each dhyāna has its own pleasure:

items: the first, **joy and bliss born of seclusion** (離生喜樂);
the second, **joy and bliss born of concentration** (定生喜樂);

the third, **the sublime bliss free of joy** (離喜妙樂). Both teachers: the highest pleasure in the three realms. Master Cháng Bǎi's image: joy is like a swimmer bobbing up and down; the third dhyāna's bliss is like being fully submerged;

the fourth, **the still bliss of purified equanimity and mindfulness** (捨念清淨寂靜無動之樂). Master Cháng Bǎi: this "bliss" is not pleasant feeling at all; the feeling is neutral and the mind utterly still. It is called bliss only nominally.

blocks.text: The formless gods enjoy "the most utterly still pleasure of release". Venerable Miào Jìng explains why some meditators want to be rid of form: they feel the body "like a sparrow in a cage".

subs.head: Six factors that intensify suffering and pleasure

blocks.text: Suffering grows more intense through six factors: bodily size, softness, conditions, duration, mind, and the underlying basis. Master Cháng Bǎi: the lower the realm, the larger the body, so the greater the area that suffers; the softer the body, the sharper the pain. "Mind" means the mind's lack of discernment: the less one understands, the worse one suffers. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that the same factors intensify pleasure "by the same reasoning". This is a quietly important point for practice. Understanding does not remove pain, but it changes how much we suffer from it.

Pleasure not born of noble wealth depends on four kinds of resource: delight (vehicles, clothes, ornaments, music, scents), nourishment (massage, exercise), good omen, and food. Master Cháng Bǎi notes that the "purity" of lucky objects (auspicious grass, conch shells) is really superstition: each culture has its own lucky signs.

The **seven noble treasures** (七聖財): faith, moral discipline, conscientiousness (慚), a sense of shame (愧), learning, generosity, and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi tells a story for the fourth. A father stealing turnips told his child to keep watch; the child said, "The moon is watching you", and the father, ashamed, put the turnip down. Conscientiousness is self-respect; shame is regard for others, even for heaven and earth.

subs.head: Fifteen ways noble wealth is better

blocks.text: The treatise contrasts the two kinds of wealth fifteen times. Ordinary wealth's pleasure is not always present, since it depends on external conditions; noble wealth's is, since it depends on internal ones. Ordinary wealth exists only in the desire realm; noble wealth in all three realms and beyond. Ordinary wealth is "exhaustible and has a limit". Master Cháng Bǎi: however many clothes you own, you can wear only one or two at a time, but study of the Dharma only grows richer.

Ordinary wealth "cannot be carried into the next life". Venerable Miào Jìng tells of a king who hoarded gold and died with a coin in his mouth, meaning to take it with him; it stayed in his mouth. And ordinary wealth's pleasure is unreal, "like scabies": Venerable Miào Jìng explains that scratching an itch feels good, but it is the disease that makes it feel good.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what pleasure do gods reborn in the first dhyāna experience?
options: joy and bliss born of concentration
the sublime bliss free of joy
joy and bliss born of seclusion
the still, unmoving bliss of purified equanimity and mindfulness
quiz.why: "The gods reborn in the first dhyāna of the form realm experience that very ground's joy and bliss born of seclusion." A is the second dhyāna, B the third, D the fourth. Master Cháng Bǎi: one reaches the first dhyāna step by step from desire-realm and access concentration, then aspires to be reborn there; weak, middling, and superior concentration lead to Brahmā's Retinue, Ministers, and Great Brahmā.

quiz.q: Third-dhyāna gods experience "the sublime bliss free of joy." How do both teachers rank it?
options: the most excellent pleasure in all three realms — none higher
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The sūtras and treatises say the third dhyāna's bliss is the most excellent in the three realms; there is no higher bliss." Master Cháng Bǎi: its beings are "wholly immersed in pleasant feeling, without the surge of joy — a more excellent bliss." The fourth is higher but not "most blissful," since it has left pleasant feeling behind (see Q1-4). D is wrong: the third dhyāna is still contaminated.

quiz.q: Fourth-dhyāna gods experience "the still, unmoving bliss of purified equanimity and mindfulness." According to Master Cháng Bǎi, is this "bliss" a pleasant feeling?
options: no — pleasant feeling is gone; it is accompanied by neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling, the mind utterly still, and is called "bliss" only nominally
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "This 'bliss' is not pleasant feeling, for pleasant feeling has been cut off; it is accompanied by neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the mind utterly still and unmoving — called bliss in name only." Venerable Miào Jìng adds that the fourth dhyāna has no in- or out-breath, and is free of inner calamities (applied and sustained thought, joy, pleasure, breath) and outer ones (water, fire, wind).

quiz.q: The treatise names six factors by which suffering and pleasure intensify. Which is NOT among them?
quiz.why: The six: bodily size, softness, conditions, duration, mind, and underlying basis. "Merit" is not one. Master Cháng Bǎi: the higher the realm, the longer the life and the longer the pleasure; the lower, the larger the body and the greater the area of suffering.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the seven kinds of noble wealth?
options: faith, moral discipline, conscientiousness, a sense of shame, learning, generosity, wisdom
quiz.why: "Faith, moral discipline, conscientiousness, a sense of shame, learning, generosity, and wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: the *Pixunji* explains them following the *Saṅgītiparyāya*, fascicle 16, and he quotes the verse "Through much learning one knows the Dharma; through much learning one keeps far from evil." Venerable Miào Jìng: a practitioner lacking these seven "is called a great thief of the world."

quiz.q: The text says ordinary wealth's pleasure is not present at all times, while noble wealth's is. Why?
options: the first depends on external conditions, the second on internal ones
noble wealth exists only in heaven
quiz.why: "Non-noble wealth's pleasure is not present at all times, since it depends on external conditions; noble wealth's pleasure is present at all times, since it depends on internal conditions." Master Cháng Bǎi: "As long as one keeps right mindfulness in each instant, each instant is happy — it rests on inner conditions, needing no one else." B is a different contrast (being seized).

quiz.q: Venerable Miào Jìng tells of a king who hoarded wealth and died with a coin in his mouth. Which of the fifteen contrasts does it illustrate?
options: ordinary wealth's pleasure cannot be carried into the next life
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the king meant to take his money with him, but "it didn't go — it was still in his mouth," and the story awakened a king. The text: "Non-noble wealth's pleasure cannot be carried from this life into the next; noble wealth's pleasure can." Nearby he cites the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*: enjoying worldly pleasure is like drinking salt water when thirsty — matching "can never be fully satisfied."
